name: CI

on:
  push:
    # Only the refs that take direct pushes and have no pull request to trigger
    # CI for them. Every other branch reaches CI through the pull_request
    # trigger below; triggering on all pushes made a branch with an open PR run
    # the whole matrix twice for the same commit (verified on sha 2e6afd5d44,
    # which produced both a push run and a pull_request run), doubling demand on
    # the runner pool.
    #
    # release/* is deliberately absent. Release branches are merged through PRs
    # (#7744 head release/2.0.64, #7841 head release/2.0.65), so listing them
    # would preserve exactly the duplication this filter removes: sha 194bd971
    # produced a push run and a pull_request run 9 seconds apart. The PR run on
    # the merge commit is the more relevant gate.
    #
    # Branches pushed without a PR (instrospect, fastjson3, android5/android8,
    # fix/* -- all verified to have zero open PRs) get no CI from this trigger.
    # Validate them by opening a PR or via workflow_dispatch. Note this includes
    # the branch carrying this very change: GitHub evaluates the pushed ref's
    # own workflow file, so this filter cannot be smoke-tested by pushing to the
    # branch that introduces it.
    #
    # `tags` must be listed explicitly: declaring only `branches` excludes tag
    # pushes altogether, and a main-line release tag is the only full-matrix run
    # between merge and publishing to Maven Central. Main-line tag pushes do run
    # this workflow today -- run 30743811143 (head_branch=2.0.64), and 2.0.63 /
    # 2.0.65 likewise. '2.*' covers those and future 2.x releases while
    # excluding the legacy 0.x/1.x tags and the fastcode_*/bak_* scratch tags.
    #
    # Scope of that claim: GitHub evaluates the workflow file at the tagged
    # commit, so this filter only governs tags cut on commits carrying this
    # file. The *.android5 / *.android8 tags are cut on the android5 / android8
    # branches, which still hold a different legacy workflow at this same path
    # (`name: Java CI`, `ubuntu-20.04`, JDK 8/11/17). That runner label is
    # retired, so those runs queue until GitHub's 24-hour cap cancels them --
    # run 33637740678 (tag 2.0.65.android8) went 13:45:57 to 13:46:00 the next
    # day, cancelled. Pre-existing gap, not a regression from this change;
    # porting this file onto android5/android8 is separate work.
    branches:
      - main
      - v2.1.x
    tags:
      - '2.*'
      - 'v2.*'  # the repo already uses a v-prefix for branches (v2.1.x), so a
                # v-prefixed release tag is plausible; missing it fails silently
                # -- no run at all -- on the release gate
    # https://docs.github.com/en/actions/using-workflows/workflow-syntax-for-github-actions#example-excluding-paths
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**.md'
  pull_request:
    paths-ignore:
      - 'docs/**'
      - '**.md'
  workflow_dispatch:

name: Checks

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  checks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      # submodules: the SoloPlay submodule cannot be checked in isolation (its tsconfig points at
      # ../../sdk and ../../libs), so the parent checkout is where it gets validated - against the
      # exact commit this repo pins.
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      # Node 24: eslint-plugin-es-x@10 requires ^22.23.0 || ^24.18.0 || >=26.4.0, and
      # eslint@10 requires ^20.19.0 || ^22.13.0 || >=24. Anything older cannot run the toolchain.
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      # lint:check, never `lint` - that one is `eslint --fix`, which would rewrite files in CI
      # and let anything auto-fixable pass silently.
      - name: ESLint
        run: npm run lint:check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      # The no-undef inventory is generated. If someone adds a global without regenerating,
      # the committed file goes stale and no-undef quietly stops covering it.
      - name: Globals inventory is current
        run: npm run globals:check

      - name: Typecheck (SoloPlay submodule)
        run: npm run typecheck:soloplay

      # Every runtime .js must belong to a TS program. A file in none gets no typechecking and
      # no editor intellisense, and nothing else reports it.
      - name: No orphaned files
        run: node tools/audit/program-files.mjs --check

Cancel superseded runs

Pattern: P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE (stale_run_cancellation)

When is cancel superseded runs applicable?

Assess cancel superseded runs for this repository, preserve its required checks, and propose a minimal change or NO_CHANGE.

Preconditions: Runs represent the same workflow and branch or PR; A newer revision supersedes older checks

Contraindications: Release or deployment work; Distinct branches share a cancellation group

Method: Partition cancellation by workflow and branch/PR; Preserve run identity and audit records

Reported finding: Superseding runs can reduce duplicate work.

Reported metrics: {"vm_time_reduction_percent": {"free": 1.9, "paid": 4.1}}

Source: Resource Usage and Optimization Opportunities in Workflows of GitHub Actions (2024), 4.2.3; Table 4; PDF pp. 7: https://software-lab.org/publications/icse2024_workflows.pdf

finish every revision's CI run


Literature example after:
